1.  Strength training:  You can use a resistance band to add resistance to your strength training, which will help you build strength and muscle more quickly.  Here’s how:

Sit on the ground with your knees bent and knees facing forward.  Wrap the ends of the resistance band around your thighs, just above your knee.  Hold the tension with your hands and feet.

2.  Stretching:  There are so many different stretches you can do with a resistance band, but here are some ideas:

1)  Calf Raises:  Step onto the resistance band with your right foot and hold for a second.  Then switch and repeat with your left foot.  It’s great to start with your feet next to each other for this, but if you aren’t comfortable with that, you can keep the resistance band at the side of the floor.

2)  Spiderman:  Wrap the resistance band around your legs and pull it towards your body.  When you feel the band stretch the width of your leg, start jumping and spiking your feet up and back.  You can do this for 30 seconds or so, and alternate legs.  You’ll feel strong and toned after you do this a few times.

3)  Lunges:  Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, then step to one side with your right foot.  Wrap the band around your right leg and lean towards the wall, keeping your back leg straight.  Hold for a second, then switch and repeat with your left leg. 
3)  Agility drills:  A very common agility drill is the “fireman’s carry”.  This will improve your speed and ability to get your feet beneath you quickly.  Set up two cones about 20-30 feet apart, and walk forward between the cones, passing the first cone to your partner as you go.  As you walk past, keep your arms in a “C” shape. 
4)  Pivots & bridges:  This will strengthen your glutes and hamstrings.  Sit on the floor with your legs bent and your knees to one side.  Wrap the ends of the resistance band around your shins just above your knee.  Keeping your knees together, hinge forward from your hips, lifting your feet off the floor.  Then lower back down.  Repeat for 10-15 reps.  You can also do this with just one leg, or stand on the resistance band and lift your left leg, then do the same with your right leg. 
5)  Band Push-ups:  These will definitely work your chest and triceps, and are pretty easy to do.  With your forearms on the ground, grab the ends of the band and push yourself into the air.  If you want to make it more challenging, you can hold the tension on your body, rather than your hands.  Then you can push yourself up even higher. 
6)  Squats:  Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.  Push your hips back and down, then push through your heels and return to the starting position.  Repeat for 12-15 reps.  This will also work your glutes and hamstrings.
7)  Dips:  Grab a sturdy table or box, then lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the ground.  Walk your hands forward until your shoulders are above the ground, then lower yourself back down.  You can do this on your back or your side, if that’s easier.
8)  Wall push-ups:  Stand facing a wall with your hands on it, fingers pointing towards the ceiling.  Walk your feet forward until your body is parallel to the ground, then quickly lower yourself back to the starting position.
